Expected departure and countdown

Calculate the end of your day from arrival.

Set work and break hours, then view remaining time in one of five formats.

Mac 1.5.15 build31 · Windows 1.5.13
OverviewHow to useExampleScope and limitsRelated features

Expected departure is calculated

The app adds configured work and break time to today’s arrival. The default is eight work hours plus one break hour. A half day or reduction uses its own calculation.

The Mac 1.5.15 menu bar shows expected departure. Its remaining-time format preference applies to the countdown in Work settings. Windows 1.5.13 shows remaining time in Today and the tray tooltip.

Set hours and a display format

  1. Open Settings → Work and set work and break time.
  2. Check today’s arrival and workday mode.
  3. In General, choose milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or hours/minutes. On Windows, use the Remaining time until departure preference.
  4. On Mac, check expected departure in the menu bar and remaining time in Work settings. On Windows, check Today and the tray tooltip.

The preference survives restart. Hours round up to one decimal place; changing format does not change the expected departure itself.

Arrive at 09:00, expect to leave at 18:00

On a regular day without a reduction, default settings give 18:00 for a 09:00 arrival. At 16:30, 90 minutes remain, displayed as 1.5 hours in hours mode. At 17:30, 30 minutes become 0.5 hours.

Automatic regular work on the last Friday gives 16:00 with the same settings. A half day is four hours without another Friday reduction. Explicitly choosing regular on Mac also removes the last-Friday reduction.

Actual departure and extra time

No arrival or Day off means no active calculation for today. Mac’s leave choice also pauses the countdown. Recheck expected departure after editing a time or setting.

Extra elapsed time appears from 30 minutes after expected departure. The meal-time guide uses expected departure plus two hours. It does not approve overtime or meal payments.

The countdown follows the app’s calculation. It does not measure breaks taken or when you left, and it does not create an actual departure record.
